note: Hearing the 4th and 5th chords move away from home, two ways: a backing track that takes turns with the chord boxes lit (the chords counted the long way once, as chord tokens), then the ear game with the answer checked. The key is moves (any key), so the first section names the key only as a param and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same; the game names its buttons as they show (IV, V, Replay, Next). Folds in the older listening-only drill of the same step.

exercise.title: Name the 4th or the 5th chord
exercise.why: The 1st chord plays first every time, so you hear the second chord as a move away from home: the 4th chord moves away, the 5th chord pulls back, and that move sounds the same in every key.

cells.text:
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on the 1st note of the scale. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on the 4th note, and {{chord:V}} is the 5th chord, built on the 5th note.
Press Play below to start the backing track in {{=key}}: {{chord:I}} and {{chord:IV}} take turns, then {{chord:I}} and {{chord:V}}. Say 4 on every {{chord:IV}} and 5 on every {{chord:V}}, with the lit chord box to help.
Listen for how the 4th chord moves away from home and the 5th chord pulls back to it.
{{?key}}In another key the chords have other names, and the 4th chord still moves away while the 5th chord still pulls back.

Press Start in the game below to hear two chords: the 1st chord, then the 4th or the 5th chord, in a new key each time. Pick IV for the 4th chord or V for the 5th chord.
Press Replay to hear the two chords again before you pick. Press Next for two new chords.
Practice until you know the answer before the second chord has faded.
